analysis:
The PR changes a single line in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 1687): a new table row documenting the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP environment variable. The variable is forwarded to the daemon. Per the doc, `0` disables the load-time shape warmup and `always` skips the shader-cache probe. It is read in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift (`shapeWarmupEnvironmentKey`). This is documentation only, so no security controls change. The supplied base text covers only the earlier part of the file (lines 1-846). The patch's changed line (~1687) is outside it, so I could not verify it in the supplied units. The patch excerpt shows the added row in full and I relied on that.

Related threats: T-041, the prefix-cache TTFT timing oracle (SEC-035, accepted). A load-time shape warmup touches TTFT behavior, but the doc only describes load-time warmup and a shader-cache probe, not per-request cache hit/miss timing. I found no evidence that it changes the cache-hit/miss oracle, the cache scoping, the TTL, or the at-rest artifacts. The variable is an operator-controlled local environment setting and crosses no trust boundary, so it adds no new attack surface. Open integration question: the implementing code (ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift) is not in this batch. If it was changed to add a new environment-forwarding path or to alter the timing of warmup relative to request admission, a reviewer of that file should check it. The documentation alone gives no cause for concern.
